01.actor: A woman selling belts and a man who snatched one
01.event: A man snatched a belt from a woman selling belts and, when she demanded it back, asked if she would be betrothed to him if he returned it; she took it and stayed silent.
01.turn: Her silence looked like consent to betrothal.
01.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled she was not betrothed, since she could say she simply took back her own property.
01.summary: A woman was selling belts when a man grabbed one from her. She told him to give it back, and he asked whether, if he did, she would be betrothed to him. She took the belt and said nothing. Rav Nahman ruled that her silence proved nothing: she could say she was only taking back what was hers.

02.actor: The daughter-in-law of Nakdimon ben Guryon
02.event: The Sages allotted the widowed daughter-in-law of Nakdimon ben Guryon two se'a of wine a week just for cooking pudding.
02.turn: She blessed them that they should allot the same to their own daughters, but she was a widow awaiting levirate marriage.
02.outcome: The Sages did not answer amen to her blessing, not wanting their daughters to share her plight.
02.summary: After her husband died, the Sages set the support of Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter-in-law at two se'a of wine each week, only for cooking. In gratitude she blessed them: may you allot the same for your own daughters. Because she was a widow waiting on her brother-in-law, the Sages declined to answer amen.

03.event: During a time of divine anger and famine, the Sages asked Rav Yosef to pray for mercy.
03.turn: He pointed out that Elisha, who fed 2,200 scholars, did not pray in a time of anger.
03.outcome: He refused to pray, asking how he could do what Elisha did not.
03.summary: In Rav Yosef's time there was a famine seen as divine anger. The Sages urged him to pray for mercy. He answered that the prophet Elisha, who supported 2,200 scholars, did not pray in such a time, so how could he? He declined.

04.actor: A man who betrothed a minor girl; Ravina
04.event: A man betrothed a minor girl in the marketplace with a bundle of vegetables, without her father's consent.
04.turn: The question was whether the father might have approved the betrothal.
04.outcome: Ravina ruled there was no concern, since the betrothal was done in a degrading manner.
04.summary: A man betrothed a young girl in the marketplace using a bundle of vegetables, without her father's approval. Ravina ruled that even those who worry a father may have approved a betrothal would not worry here, because no father would approve such a degrading betrothal. The betrothal was disregarded.

05.actor: A man who betrothed a woman conditionally, and the Sages
05.event: A man betrothed a woman on a condition and then had relations with her.
05.turn: The Sages could not rule the betrothal void.
05.outcome: The Sages could not let her leave without a bill of divorce.
05.summary: Rav Kahana, citing Ulla, reports that a man once betrothed a woman conditionally and then lived with her. The Sages did not have the power to release her without a bill of divorce, so a divorce was required.
05.missing: The details of the incident: who was involved and what the condition was; the report is a bare mention.

06.event: Levi recited five wedding blessings at the wedding of Rabbi's son, and Rav Asi recited six at the wedding of Rav Ashi's son.
06.summary: Levi visited Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's house during his son Rabbi Shimon's wedding and recited five of the wedding blessings. Rav Asi visited Rav Ashi's house during his son Mar's wedding and recited six.
06.missing: Any turn or consequence; these are two bare reports of a practice.

07.actor: Rav Yosef, Abaye, and a daughter seeking support
07.event: A case came before Rav Yosef, who told the heirs to support the daughter from dates drying on mats.
07.turn: Abaye objected that not even a creditor may collect from orphans' movable property.
07.outcome: Rav Yosef explained he meant dates still attached to the tree, and defended this again when Abaye pressed.
07.summary: A case about a daughter's support came before Rav Yosef, who told the dead man's sons to give her dates that were drying on mats. Abaye challenged him: a creditor could not collect that way, so why should she? Rav Yosef clarified that he meant ripe dates still on the tree, and when Abaye pressed again, he said he meant dates that still needed the tree.
07.missing: Whether the daughter actually received anything; the exchange ends as legal argument.

08.actor: A betrothed couple and Rav Yosef
08.event: A betrothed man and his pregnant betrothed came before Rav Yosef; she said the child was his, and he agreed.
08.outcome: Rav Yosef ruled there was nothing to be concerned about, since he admitted it and the law follows Rabban Gamliel in any case.
08.summary: A betrothed couple came before Rav Yosef because she was pregnant. She said she had conceived from him, and he confirmed it. Rav Yosef ruled there was no cause for concern: the man admitted paternity, and even otherwise her word would be believed.

09.event: Visiting Neharde'a, Rav Avya saw a man tying a door bolt with a reed.
09.turn: He judged the reed an inadequate fastening.
09.outcome: He ruled that the door may not be locked with it on Shabbat.
09.summary: Rav Avya came to Neharde'a and saw a man fastening a door bolt to the door with a reed. He ruled that this door could not be locked with that bolt on Shabbat, because the reed did not properly attach the bolt.

10.event: Rabbi Hanina sent his weekly four dinars to a pauper by his wife's hand.
10.turn: She overheard the household asking whether he would dine on silver or gold tablecloths, and reported he did not need charity.
10.outcome: Rabbi Hanina quoted Rabbi Elazar: we should be grateful to swindlers, since they excuse our failures to the truly poor.
10.summary: Rabbi Hanina used to send a poor man four dinars every Friday. One week his wife delivered it and came back saying the man did not need charity: she had heard his household ask whether he would eat on silver or gold tablecloths. Rabbi Hanina responded with Rabbi Elazar's saying that we should appreciate swindlers, for without them we would be sinning daily against the truly poor.

11.event: A dispute about a child's gift was sent to Rav Mordekhai with its attributions reversed.
11.turn: Rav Mordekhai recalled asking Rav Ashi, who stood with one foot on the step, and Rav Ashi said a child's gift is valid.
11.outcome: Rav Mordekhai sent word to Mar bar Rav Ashi reminding him of the incident.
11.summary: Two sages disagreed whether a young child's gift is valid, and the opinions were reported to Rav Mordekhai with the names swapped. He sent word to Mar bar Rav Ashi: wasn't it so that when your father stood with one foot on the ground and one on the step, we asked him, and he said a child's gift is valid in every case?
11.missing: How Mar bar Rav Ashi responded to the message.

12.actor: An Amorite and a resident of Eretz Yisrael
12.event: An Amorite asked a resident of the Land how many dates the palm on the Jordan bank yields, and was told sixty kor.
12.turn: The Amorite scoffed that in his people's day it yielded 120, so the newcomers had ruined the land.
12.outcome: The resident answered that he had spoken of only one side of the tree.
12.summary: An Amorite asked a man from the Land of Israel how much fruit they harvested from a palm by the Jordan. Sixty kor, the man said. The Amorite mocked him: you have barely arrived and already ruined it, since we used to take 120. The man replied that he was only counting one side of the tree.

13.actor: Ravina and his host in Mehoza
13.event: In Mehoza, Ravina's host showed him a slaughtering knife, and Ravina sent him to show it to Rava.
13.turn: The host asked why, since Rava allows a scholar to check a knife for himself.
13.outcome: Ravina replied that he was only buying the meat, so it was not slaughter for himself.
13.summary: Ravina visited Mehoza, Rava's town, and his host showed him a slaughtering knife to check. Ravina told him to take it to Rava. The host asked why, since Rava rules a scholar may check a knife for himself. Ravina answered that he was merely buying meat from the host, so the rule did not apply.

14.event: Faced with Rav Hamnuna's challenge, Rava fell silent.
14.turn: After Rav Hamnuna left, Rava thought of an answer, doubted it, and then confirmed it from a baraita.
14.outcome: He concluded the challenge could be answered as Rabbi Elazar's view.
14.summary: Rav Hamnuna challenged Rava with a baraita, and Rava had no answer. Once Rav Hamnuna left, Rava reproached himself for not saying the baraita follows Rabbi Elazar. He then doubted whether Rabbi Elazar held so in this kind of case, and finally recalled a baraita showing that he did.
14.missing: The start of the exchange, Rav Hamnuna's original question and Rava's position, comes before the segments shown.

15.event: A never-married man told Rav Nahman that he found his bride without signs of virginity.
15.turn: His claim revealed experience he should not have had.
15.outcome: Rav Nahman ordered him flogged, since he must have been with prostitutes.
15.summary: A man who had never been married came to Rav Nahman and claimed his bride was not a virgin. Rav Nahman ordered him flogged with palm branches: how could an unmarried man know, unless he had been with prostitutes?

16.event: Rav Ashi came to Rav Kahana's house for a wedding and recited all seven blessings on the first day.
16.outcome: On later days he recited all of them only if new guests came, and otherwise only two.
16.summary: Rav Ashi attended a wedding at Rav Kahana's house. On the first day he recited all seven wedding blessings. On the following days he recited them all only when new guests were present; otherwise he treated it as a continuation and said just two blessings.
16.missing: Any turn; the passage describes his practice over the days rather than an event that changes.

17.actor: A man who betrothed a woman in her waiting period, and Rafram
17.event: A man betrothed a woman within three months of her divorce or widowhood and then fled.
17.outcome: Rafram ruled that his flight was punishment enough, and he was not excommunicated.
17.summary: A man betrothed a woman during the three-month waiting period after her previous marriage ended, and then ran away. When the case came up, Rafram ruled that his running away was sufficient and no further penalty was needed.
17.missing: Details of the actual incident; it is a bare report attached to a stated dispute.

18.actor: A herdsman of orphans' cattle, a creditor, and Rav Nahman
18.event: A creditor seized an ox from a herdsman tending orphans' cattle; the creditor said he took it while the debtor lived, the herdsman said after his death.
18.turn: Rav Nahman asked if the herdsman had witnesses to the seizure, and he had none.
18.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled for the creditor, who could have claimed he bought the ox.
18.summary: A creditor took an ox from a herdsman caring for orphans' cattle. The creditor claimed he took it while their father was alive; the herdsman said it was after his death. Before Rav Nahman, the herdsman admitted he had no witnesses to the seizure, so Rav Nahman ruled that the creditor was believed, since he could even have claimed he had bought it.

19.event: A woman named Me'oret made her slave do three of the dangerous acts.
19.summary: A woman named Me'oret made her slave perform three of the acts said to be deadly together, and he died. The Gemara explains that he was weak.
19.missing: Any detail of the event; it is a bare report cited in a legal discussion.
